text:
Choose the correct statement considering the underlined adjectives in the text and their correct degrees according to the context:

Drill Sergeant Mendonça barked orders to the Signal Corps students like a mad dog. Today's training was (demanding) than yesterday's, pushing the will-be NCO’s to their limits. The Signal Corps students are sure they are the (smart) bunch in academic disciplines, but they also needed to excel in their physical training. Mendonça, (mean) as a rattlesnake, kept reminding them of the consequences of failing the fitness test.

The obstacle course was the (bad) of all the exercises. They climbed walls, slogged through mud, and crawled under barbed wire, sweating like pigs. By lunchtime, they were exhausted and (hungry) than wolves. Sergeant Mendonça, however, would not let us rest. "This is not a picnic, gentlemen!" he yelled. The NCO academy is not for the faint of heart in fact, but the students are determined to make it.
options: The correct form of “smart” is “the most smart”.
“The worse” is the right form for “bad”.
The correct form of the adjective “mean” is “as mean”.
subject: Inglês
explanation:
(A) (A forma correta de “smart” é “the most smart”.)
Incorreta.
“Smart” é um adjetivo curto (uma sílaba) e, portanto, seu superlativo é formado com -est, não com most.
O correto seria the smartest bunch (o grupo mais inteligente).
Logo, “the most smart” está errado.

(B) (“The worse” é a forma correta para “bad”.)
Incorreta.
A forma superlativa de “bad” é the worst, e não the worse.
Worse é o comparativo, não o superlativo.
No contexto - “The obstacle course was the (bad) of all the exercises.” -
a forma correta é the worst of all the exercises (o pior de todos os exercícios).

(C) (“Demanding” torna-se “most demanding” no contexto.)
Incorreta.
O texto diz:

"Today's training was (demanding) than yesterday's."
A estrutura pede o comparativo, não o superlativo, pois há comparação entre “today” e “yesterday”.
Logo, o correto é more demanding than yesterday’s (mais exigente que o de ontem), e não most demanding.

(D) (“Hungryer” é a forma correta de “hungry”.)
Incorreta.
O comparativo correto de “hungry” é hungrier, e não hungryer.
No texto:

"By lunchtime, they were exhausted and (hungry) than wolves."
A forma correta seria hungrier than wolves (mais famintos que lobos).
Logo, a alternativa está errada por erro ortográfico na formação do comparativo.

(E) (A forma correta do adjetivo “mean” é “as mean”.)
Correta.
O trecho diz:

"Mendonça, (mean) as a rattlesnake..."
Aqui temos uma comparação de igualdade (as...as), e a forma correta é as mean as a rattlesnake (tão malvado quanto uma cascavel).
Portanto, esta é a opção correta.
